findings.title: Test setup replaces enabled features with an immutable list
findings.body: `kc.getSpec().getFeatureSpec().setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()))` replaces any already-configured enabled features with a new immutable list. If the base Keycloak CR used for tests already enables other features, they are silently dropped. If later test or operator code tries to modify the enabled-features list, it will throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. Appending to the existing list or using a mutable list would be safer.

findings.title: No test covers operator behavior when update strategy is set without the preview feature
findings.body: The documentation added in this PR states that the operator will fail if the `rolling-updates` preview feature is not enabled, but the integration test only sets `spec.update.strategy` when it also enables the feature. There is no negative test that sets an update strategy while leaving `rolling-updates` disabled and asserts that the operator rejects or fails the CR. Without such a test, the feature-gating behavior can regress unnoticed.

findings.title: Changing recreate exit code from 4 to 3 breaks the documented command contract
findings.body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` is changed from 4 to 3, while 4 is repurposed as `FEATURE_DISABLED`. The update-compatibility documentation tells users to rely on the command exit code for automation. If the previous exit code was already consumed by scripts or CI pipelines, this change can cause existing automation to misinterpret a recreate result as feature-disabled, or vice versa, unless this is explicitly treated as a breaking change and documented.

findings.title: Non-zero exit codes are not verified
findings.body: The PR introduces or changes meaningful exit codes (0, 3, 4), but the distribution tests do not assert them. `testFeatureNotEnabled` only checks the error message and does not verify exit code 4, and `testWrongVersions` does not verify exit code 3. Since the documentation presents these exit codes as a contract for automation, regressions in the exit-code behavior would not be caught.
